name: Private Limited Company Registration
meta_title: Private Limited Company Registration Online in India
meta_description: Register your private limited company online with CA support. Name approval, DSC, DIN, MCA filing and PAN in 7 to 10 days. Upload documents online or on WhatsApp.
excerpt: Register a private limited company online with complete CA support, from name approval to certificate of incorporation, PAN and TAN.
intro: A private limited company is the most trusted business structure in India. Investors prefer it, banks lend to it comfortably and customers take it seriously. It gives your business a separate legal identity and protects your personal assets through limited liability.

Krishna TaxNova registers your company completely online. You fill in your details, upload your documents on this page or WhatsApp them to us, and our CA team handles name approval, digital signatures and all MCA filings until your certificate of incorporation is in your inbox.
what: Private limited company registration is the process of incorporating a company under the Companies Act, 2013 through the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA). The company needs at least two directors and two shareholders, who can be the same people. Registration is done through the SPICe+ form, which also covers PAN, TAN, EPFO, ESIC and bank account opening in a single application.
Once registered, the company exists as a separate legal person. It can own property, open bank accounts, sign contracts and raise funding in its own name, independent of its owners.
who: Startups planning to raise funding from angel investors or venture capital
Founders who want limited liability and a clear separation between personal and business assets
Family businesses moving from proprietorship to a corporate structure
NRIs and foreign nationals investing in an Indian business
Service providers and manufacturers who bid for contracts that require a registered company
benefits: Limited Liability Protection
Your personal savings and property stay protected. Liability is limited to the amount you invest in shares.
Separate Legal Identity
The company can buy assets, borrow and enter contracts in its own name, independent of the founders.
Easier Funding
Investors and banks prefer private limited companies because shareholding and governance are clearly defined.
Perpetual Existence
The company continues even if directors or shareholders change, which keeps the business stable.
Brand Credibility
The Pvt Ltd tag builds instant trust with customers, vendors and large clients.
Employee Stock Options
You can attract and retain talent by offering ESOPs, which is not possible in a proprietorship or partnership.
documents: PAN card of all directors and shareholders
Aadhaar card of all directors
Passport size photograph of each director
Identity proof: voter ID, passport or driving license
Address proof: latest bank statement or utility bill (not older than 2 months)
Registered office proof: electricity bill or property tax receipt
Rent agreement and NOC from the owner if the office is rented
Proposed company names and brief description of business activity
process: Free Consultation and Name Check
We discuss your business, suggest the right structure and check the availability of your proposed company names on the MCA portal.
Document Collection
Upload your documents on this page or WhatsApp them to us. Our team verifies everything and prepares the incorporation paperwork.
Digital Signatures and Name Approval
We obtain DSC for the directors and file the name reservation through SPICe+ Part A.
Incorporation Filing
We draft the MOA and AOA and file SPICe+ Part B along with AGILE-PRO for PAN, TAN, EPFO and ESIC.
Certificate of Incorporation
MCA issues the certificate with CIN, PAN and TAN. We help you open the bank account and start compliant operations.
validity: Lifetime, subject to annual ROC filings
fees_note: Government fees depend on authorised capital and state stamp duty
why_us: We have incorporated companies for founders across India and we stay with you after registration for accounting, GST and ROC compliance, so you are never left searching for a new consultant at every step.
faqs: How many people are needed to start a private limited company?
You need a minimum of two directors and two shareholders. The same two people can hold both roles. At least one director must be a resident of India.
Is there a minimum capital requirement?
No. There is no minimum paid up capital requirement. Many companies start with a small capital such as ten thousand rupees and increase it later as the business grows.
Can I register the company at my home address?
Yes. A residential address can be used as the registered office. You only need a utility bill and a no objection certificate from the property owner.
What compliance is needed after incorporation?
The company must appoint an auditor, maintain accounts, file annual returns with the ROC and file an income tax return every year. Our team manages all of this under one plan.

name: LLP Registration
meta_title: LLP Registration Online in India | Limited Liability Partnership
meta_description: Register your LLP online with CA experts. Name approval, DSC, FiLLiP filing and LLP agreement in 7 to 10 days. Low cost, low compliance. WhatsApp us your documents.
excerpt: Start a limited liability partnership that combines the flexibility of a partnership with the safety of limited liability.
intro: A limited liability partnership (LLP) gives you the freedom of a traditional partnership with the protection of limited liability. It is a popular choice for professional firms, consultants, agencies and family businesses that want a formal structure without heavy compliance.

Krishna TaxNova completes your LLP registration fully online. Share your details and documents through the form on this page or on WhatsApp, and our team handles everything from name reservation to the LLP agreement.
what: An LLP is registered under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. It needs at least two designated partners, and there is no upper limit on the number of partners. The rights and duties of partners are set out in the LLP agreement, which is filed with the MCA after incorporation.
Unlike a private limited company, an LLP has no board meetings, no statutory audit until turnover crosses forty lakh rupees and no dividend distribution formalities, which keeps running costs low.
who: Professional service firms such as consultants, designers, architects and IT service providers
Two or more founders who want limited liability without company level compliance
Existing partnership firms that want to upgrade to a safer structure
Businesses that do not plan to raise venture capital in the near future
benefits: Limited Liability
Each partner's risk is limited to the agreed contribution. Personal assets stay protected from business losses.
Low Compliance Cost
No mandatory audit until turnover crosses the threshold, fewer filings and no board meeting requirements.
Flexible Internal Structure
Profit sharing, roles and responsibilities are defined by the LLP agreement, exactly as the partners want.
Separate Legal Entity
The LLP can own property, sue and be sued in its own name, independent of the partners.
No Minimum Capital
You can start an LLP with any amount of contribution, even a few thousand rupees.
documents: PAN card of all partners
Aadhaar card of all partners
Photograph of each partner
Address proof of partners: bank statement or utility bill not older than 2 months
Registered office proof: electricity bill or property tax receipt
Rent agreement and NOC from the owner if the premises are rented
Proposed LLP names and nature of business
process: Consultation and Name Reservation
We confirm that an LLP suits your plans and reserve your preferred name through the RUN-LLP service.
Documents and Digital Signatures
You upload documents online or WhatsApp them to us. We arrange DSC for the designated partners.
Incorporation Filing
We prepare and file the FiLLiP form with the MCA for incorporation and DPIN allotment.
LLP Agreement Drafting
Our team drafts a clear LLP agreement covering capital, profit sharing and duties, executed on stamp paper.
Agreement Filing and PAN
We file Form 3 within 30 days of incorporation and obtain PAN and TAN so you can open the bank account.
fees_note: Government fees depend on contribution amount and state stamp duty on the agreement
why_us: We draft LLP agreements that actually protect partners, covering exit, dispute resolution and profit sharing clearly, instead of using a thin template that fails when you need it.
faqs: What is the difference between an LLP and a private limited company?

An LLP is simpler and cheaper to run, with fewer filings and no audit until turnover crosses the limit. A private limited company is better for raising equity funding. If investors are on your roadmap, choose the company; otherwise an LLP is usually more economical.
Is audit compulsory for an LLP?
Audit becomes mandatory only when annual turnover exceeds forty lakh rupees or contribution exceeds twenty five lakh rupees. Below these limits the LLP simply files its annual forms.
Can an existing partnership firm be converted into an LLP?
Yes. A registered partnership firm can convert into an LLP by filing Form 17 along with the incorporation forms. We handle the entire conversion including intimation to authorities.
What are the annual filings for an LLP?
Every LLP files Form 11 (annual return) by 30 May and Form 8 (statement of accounts) by 30 October, along with its income tax return. We send reminders and file these for you.

name: One Person Company Registration

meta_description: Register a One Person Company online with CA support. Single founder, limited liability, full corporate identity. Documents online or on WhatsApp, done in 7 to 10 days.
excerpt: Get a full corporate identity with limited liability as a single founder through a One Person Company.
intro: A One Person Company (OPC) lets a single entrepreneur own a company with limited liability and a proper corporate identity. It is the ideal upgrade from a sole proprietorship when you want credibility with clients and protection for personal assets.
With Krishna TaxNova, OPC registration is fully online. Fill in your details, upload your documents or send them on WhatsApp, and our CA team completes the incorporation with the MCA.
what: An OPC is a private company with only one shareholder, registered under the Companies Act, 2013. The sole member appoints a nominee who takes over ownership if the member is unable to continue. The OPC enjoys separate legal status, its own PAN and the same contract making powers as any other company.
who: Solo founders, consultants and freelancers who want a corporate structure
Proprietors whose clients or vendors ask for a registered company
Single owners who want limited liability without adding a co-founder
Professionals building a personal brand into a scalable business
benefits: Single Owner, Full Control
You take every decision without needing a second shareholder or partner.
Limited Liability
Business risks stay in the company. Your personal assets remain safe.
Corporate Credibility
An OPC signs contracts and raises invoices as a company, which builds trust with larger clients.
Easy Conversion
An OPC can be converted into a private limited company later when you add co-founders or investors.
Fewer Compliance Requirements
OPCs enjoy relaxations such as no requirement to hold an annual general meeting.

PAN card and Aadhaar card of the nominee with a signed consent (Form INC-3)
Photograph of the owner and nominee

Registered office proof with NOC from the property owner
Proposed company names and business activity details

We confirm that OPC is the right fit and explain the nominee requirement.
Documents and DSC

Name Reservation

Incorporation Filing

Certificate and Bank Account

validity: Lifetime, subject to annual ROC filings
fees_note: Government fees depend on authorised capital and state stamp duty
why_us: We guide you honestly on OPC versus proprietorship versus private limited, based on your revenue, clients and plans, so you do not pay for a structure you do not need.
faqs: Who can register an OPC in India?
Only an Indian citizen who is a resident of India can incorporate an OPC. A person can hold only one OPC at a time and must name a nominee at incorporation.
Why does an OPC need a nominee?
The nominee steps in as the member if the owner passes away or becomes incapable. This keeps the company alive and its contracts valid. The nominee's written consent is filed with the MCA.
When should an OPC convert to a private limited company?
Conversion makes sense when you want to add a co-founder, issue shares to investors or expand ownership. The conversion is voluntary and we manage the complete process.
Does an OPC pay different tax than a proprietorship?
Yes. An OPC is taxed as a company at corporate rates, while a proprietorship is taxed at individual slab rates. We run the numbers for your income level before you decide.

Krishna TaxNova drafts your partnership deed, obtains the firm's PAN and registers the firm with the Registrar of Firms, all online. You only need to share your documents through this page or on WhatsApp.

faqs: Is registration of a partnership firm compulsory?
No, a firm can operate unregistered. However, an unregistered firm cannot file a suit in court to enforce its rights, so registration is strongly recommended for any serious business.
How many partners can a firm have?
A partnership firm can have a minimum of two and a maximum of fifty partners. All partners must be competent to contract.
Can a partnership firm be converted to an LLP later?
Yes. Conversion to an LLP is common once the business grows, and it brings limited liability. We handle the full conversion process.
How is a partnership firm taxed?
The firm is taxed at a flat thirty percent on its profits. Interest and remuneration to partners are deductible within limits under section 40(b), which we structure for maximum tax efficiency.

intro: A sole proprietorship is the quickest and most economical way to start a business in India. There is no separate law for proprietorships; your identity is established through registrations such as GST, MSME Udyam and a shop and establishment license.
Krishna TaxNova sets up your proprietorship with the exact registrations you need to open a current account and start billing customers. Everything is done online through this page or WhatsApp.
what: A proprietorship is a business owned and run by one person, with no legal distinction between the owner and the business. Since there is no incorporation certificate, banks and buyers rely on government registrations in the firm's name, typically GST registration, Udyam (MSME) registration and a shop and establishment license, to recognise the business.
who: First time entrepreneurs testing a business idea
Shopkeepers, traders and local service providers
Freelancers and home based businesses that need a current account
Small businesses with turnover below GST and audit thresholds

Complete Control
You take all decisions and keep all profits.
Lower Tax at Small Scale

why_us: We register only what you need. Many agents sell unnecessary licenses to proprietors; our CA team tells you clearly what is mandatory, what is useful and what is a waste of money.
faqs: Is there a single registration certificate for a proprietorship?
No. A proprietorship is recognised through business registrations such as GST, Udyam and the shop license taken in the trade name. Banks accept any two of these to open a current account.
Do I need GST registration for my proprietorship?

GST is mandatory once turnover crosses forty lakh rupees for goods or twenty lakh for services, and for anyone selling on e-commerce platforms. Below these limits it is optional, though it helps with input credit and B2B clients.
Can I use a brand name for my proprietorship?
Yes, you can trade under any name that is not already trademarked by someone else. To protect the name legally, we recommend filing a trademark application, which we can handle for you.
What taxes does a proprietor pay?
Business profit is added to your personal income and taxed at slab rates. If turnover is within limits, presumptive taxation under section 44AD or 44ADA can reduce paperwork significantly.

Does a public limited company have to list on a stock exchange?

Can a private limited company be converted into a public limited company?

meta_title: Nidhi Company Registration Online | Mutual Benefit Company
meta_description: Register a Nidhi company for member based lending and savings. Expert help with incorporation, NDH filings and RBI exempt compliance. Documents on WhatsApp.
excerpt: Start a member based savings and lending business through a Nidhi company, without an RBI license.
intro: A Nidhi company is a mutual benefit company that accepts deposits from and lends only to its own members. It is the most accessible way to run a regulated savings and credit business in India because it does not require an RBI license.
Krishna TaxNova handles the complete setup: incorporation as a public limited company, Nidhi specific compliance and the mandatory member and fund milestones in the first year.
what: Nidhi companies are governed by section 406 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the Nidhi Rules, 2014. The company is incorporated as a public limited company with at least seven members and three directors, and must reach two hundred members and a net owned fund of twenty lakh rupees within stipulated timelines, followed by a declaration through form NDH-4.
who: Entrepreneurs who want to run a community savings and lending business
Groups running informal chit or credit circles that want a legal structure
Promoters looking for a finance business without RBI licensing
Community organisations promoting thrift among members
benefits: No RBI License Needed
Nidhi companies are exempt from RBI registration, which lowers the entry barrier for a lending business.
Member Based Safety
Business is restricted to members, which limits exposure and keeps operations manageable.
High Trust Structure
Regulated status under the Companies Act builds depositor confidence.
Low Capital Entry
Start with ten lakh rupees of equity capital and grow the fund with the business.
Simple Lending Model
Loans are secured against gold, property or deposits, keeping default risk low.

Photographs of directors
Identity and address proof of all subscribers
Registered office proof: utility bill and NOC from owner
Proposed name with Nidhi Limited as suffix
Capital structure and planned branch details
process: Consultation

Incorporation

validity: Lifetime, subject to Nidhi Rules compliance and annual filings
fees_note: Government fees depend on authorised capital; minimum equity capital is 10 lakh rupees
why_us: Nidhi rules changed significantly in recent years and many consultants still follow old procedures. Our team keeps your structure aligned with the current Nidhi (Amendment) Rules so your NDH-4 approval is not rejected.
faqs: Can a Nidhi company deal with the public?
No. A Nidhi company can accept deposits from and lend only to its registered members. Dealing with non members is a serious violation that can lead to penalties and closure.
What loans can a Nidhi company give?
Loans are given against security such as gold, silver, property or the member's own deposits. Unsecured lending and microfinance style operations are not permitted.
What is NDH-4 and why does it matter?

NDH-4 is the application for official declaration as a Nidhi company. Without this approval the company cannot legally operate as a Nidhi, so meeting the member and fund milestones on time is critical.
How many branches can a Nidhi company open?
After three years of profitable operation, a Nidhi can open up to three branches within its district. Further expansion needs regulatory approval, which we help you plan.

faqs: Who can become a member of a producer company?
Only primary producers, people or institutions engaged in producing the relevant primary produce, can be members. Proof of producer status is required at the time of joining.
What is the minimum number of members and directors?
A producer company needs at least ten individual producer members or two producer institutions, and a minimum of five directors.
Can a producer company accept deposits?
It can accept deposits only from its members in the form prescribed under the Act, not from the public. Member financing rules are specific, and we set up compliant systems for this.
Is a producer company the same as an FPO?

An FPO is the broader term for a farmer producer organisation, which can be a cooperative or a company. A producer company is the corporate form of an FPO and is the structure most schemes now prefer.

validity: Lifetime, subject to annual ROC, tax and FEMA compliance
fees_note: Government fees depend on authorised capital; apostille costs vary by country
why_us: Cross border setups fail on details: apostille formats, FEMA timelines and resident director rules. Our team has checklists for each, so your incorporation and FC-GPR filing go through without rework.
faqs: Does an Indian subsidiary need an Indian director?
Yes. At least one director must be a person resident in India. The other directors can be foreign nationals. We can advise on structuring this requirement compliantly.
Is government approval needed for foreign investment?
Most sectors fall under the automatic route where no prior approval is needed; only post facto RBI reporting applies. A few sensitive sectors need government approval, which we identify upfront.
What is FC-GPR and when is it filed?

FC-GPR is the RBI filing that reports the issue of shares to a foreign investor. It must be filed within thirty days of share allotment, along with valuation and KYC documents. Missing it attracts penalties.
Can profits be sent back to the parent company?

Yes. Dividends can be repatriated after dividend distribution formalities and applicable taxes. Fees for services and royalties can also be paid to the parent under FEMA rules with proper documentation.

intro: A Section 8 company is the most structured and credible form of NGO in India. Donors, CSR teams and international agencies prefer it because it is licensed by the central government and governed by company law discipline.

what: A Section 8 company is incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 for charitable objects such as education, health, environment, art or social welfare. It enjoys exemption from minimum capital norms and uses words like Foundation or Association instead of Private Limited in its name.

faqs: Can a Section 8 company pay salaries?
Yes. It can pay reasonable salaries to employees and professionals for services rendered, including founders working in executive roles. What it cannot do is distribute profits as dividends.
Which is better: trust, society or Section 8 company?

For CSR funds, government projects and institutional donors, Section 8 offers the strongest credibility. Trusts are simpler for small family run charities. We recommend the form that matches your funding plans.
Is 12A and 80G automatic after registration?
No. They are separate approvals from the Income Tax Department. We file both applications along with the required activity and financial documents.
Can foreigners fund a Section 8 company?
Foreign donations require FCRA registration, which is generally available after three years of activity. Until then, an FCRA prior permission route exists for specific projects.
